_about: PLACEHOLDER conversations, to show how talking and choices work until the real storylines are written. A line is [speaker id, text]; 'you' is the player. 'when' and a choice's 'if' are conditions (stage, minAge, flag, bondAtLeast, moneyAtLeast, trait...). Effects: bond, money, setFlag, traits, skills, happiness, remember. {name} is the player's name and {currency} the money's name.

lines: Good morning, my little one. Look at those eyes, {name}. Wide awake already.
Oh, that laugh. Your father had that laugh.

effects.remember: Mum said you laugh like your father.

lines: Ow! Strong grip. You'll be trouble, you will.
Always looking past me at something more interesting.
Who's my favourite? You are. Don't tell anyone.
Is that so? Fascinating. Tell me more.
Come here, little bird. Gran's got a song for you.
That's it. My mother sang me this one. One day you'll sing it too.
Ha! No rhythm at all. You'll fit right in with this family.
Alright, alright. Not a music lover. Noted.
{name}. Come and sit. Your mother works too hard, you know that?

choices.text: Why does she work so much?
Gran, can I go and play?

lines: Because things cost money, and money doesn't grow on the trees out there.
You already do, just by being a good child. But keep asking. She'll remember you asked.

effects.remember: Gran told you your mother works too hard. You asked how you could help.

lines: Go on. Childhood doesn't last. Nobody tells you that until it's gone.
My knees are telling me it'll rain.
There you are, {name}. Five years old. Did you sleep at all?

choices.text: Yes! I dreamed I could fly.
Not really. A dog barked all night.
Can I go outside to play?

lines: Fly? Then you can fly down the lane today. By yourself.
Only the lane, mind. Stay off the road and be home before dark.

effects.remember: The first day Mum let you out on Willow Lane by yourself.

lines: That dog. I'll have a word with Mrs Pell.
Go on, you can go out on the lane by yourself today. Stay off the road, and be home before dark.

effects.remember: The first day Mum let you out on Willow Lane by yourself.

lines: Already? You haven't even said good morning.
Alright. Today you can go out on Willow Lane by yourself. Only the lane, mind.
Stay off the road, say hello to Mrs Pell, and be home before dark.

effects.remember: The first day Mum let you out on Willow Lane by yourself.

lines: Mum... Mr Ambrose has new sweets at the shop.
And you have your own {currency}, don't you?

choices.text: I want to keep mine. Can you buy them?
I'll use my own. Just checking.
Can I earn some? I can sweep the yard.

effects.remember: You earned your first 5 {currency}, sweeping the yard.

lines: Keep yours, spend mine? Nice try.
Good. It's yours. Spend it how you like, but it won't come back.
Sweep it properly and there's 5 {currency} in it for you.
Back before dark, {name}. I mean it.
{name}! Your mum let you out by yourself? Finally! Now we can actually do stuff.

choices.text: I bet I can run faster than you.

lines: Yes! Nobody else on this street is our age. It's all old people and cats.

effects.remember: Your first day out alone, you and Nico ran straight to the park.

lines: You never talk much. That's okay. I talk enough for two.
No way. I'm the fastest on Willow Lane.
Bench to the lamp post. One day. You're on.

effects.remember: Nico challenged you to a race.

lines: Mr Ambrose has new sweets. The fizzy ones.
One day I'll have a shop like his. Then sweets are free. For me.
Did you see that cat? It's been sitting on the car all day.
Oh, hello dear. You're the little one from the end house.
My knees aren't what they were. Would you carry my bag to the door?
What a kind child. Your mother raised you well.
Here. Don't tell her I gave you this.
Busy. At your age. Well, off you go then.
The lane was all fields when I was your age. Fields, dear.
Welcome, welcome. What can I get you?
Good choice. Careful, they make your eyes water.
Looking is free. Buying is how I eat.
